claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help determine your eligibility, I need to start by understanding your situation.

**First, let me ask about the child you're claiming for:**

How old is the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for? The eligibility rules differ based on age:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 years or older

Please tell me the age of your child (or each child if you have multiple children), and their name(s) so I can help assess eligibility for each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. 

I have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, they fall into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to know about Alex's education or training status:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school or college, or approved training)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in approved education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is studying for A-levels at sixth form college, that's approved education. Now I need to verify that the level and nature of the education meets the requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! A-levels at sixth form college are approved non-advanced education. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - not including homework or unsupervised study)

2. **Is this education funded by an employer or part of an agreement for a future job with an employer?**

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is studying full-time - it's a regular sixth form course, not anything to do with an employer. Just normal college studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That confirms Alex is in approved non-advanced education on a full-time basis. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's fine - Alex is just focused on studies. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Tax Credits

If Alex is NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right, that's fine and we can continue.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's still living at home with me and I support him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, that's all good. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One more check about Alex's education:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?** 

Most apprenticeships disqualify from Child Benefit (though there are some exceptions for Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - he's just doing regular A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is doing regular A-levels, so that's fine. Now let me move on to checking your eligibility as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. Child Benefit has UK residency requirements, but there are several ways you can qualify.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, there are other ways to qualify (such as having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant abroad), but let's start with the simplest question.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. You can qualify in several ways:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means either:
1. **Living with Alex** (which you mentioned you do - Alex lives at home with you), OR
2. **Contributing to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least as much as the Child Benefit amount towards their care)

Since you mentioned Alex is living at home with you and you support him, it sounds like you meet this requirement. Can you confirm Alex lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

If someone else is claiming, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at a time (though you could potentially transfer the claim if they agree).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. 

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital** (as an inpatient)?
2. **In local authority care**?
3. **Being fostered**?
4. **Living normally** at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you, but I want to confirm there are no special circumstances.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is just living normally at home with me - no special circumstances like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

For example, is the council providing financial support for Alex's living costs or accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me now move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 16 years old and studying A-levels full-time at sixth form college (approved non-advanced education)
✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - Focused on studies
✅ **Alex is not receiving benefits** in their own right
✅ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - Regular A-levels
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - Living in the UK (Manchester)
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - Alex lives at home with you
✅ **No one else is claiming** Child Benefit for Alex
✅ **Alex is living normally** at home with you
✅ **The local council is not paying** towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of it back through the tax system (though you can still claim it)
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### More Information:
You can apply and find more details at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about claiming or the process?

All eligibility criteria are met.
